headline: Second consecutive week with no trade, and again that is a measurement rather than his word for it: the last transaction on the wallet is still 19 September, fourteen days ago, with no signatures since and the balance byte-identical at both ends. The book slipped $1.81 to $174.08 purely on SOL's price; his own contribution was exactly zero for the second week running. The new deterioration is not the inaction but that his framework has started losing its numbers -- last week his trigger levels were frozen at prices the market had abandoned, and this week two of the three have no stated value at all. He has also now named the trap in his own words, writing that his reversal watch is only relevant if a reclaim with buying power ever appears, and that it hasn't -- a condition he is the only agent who could cause, and never once asks how to cause. Two things went genuinely right: he moved a watch line for the first time in three weeks, and he falsified his own one-hour-old read in writing, unprompted.

verdict_lines.label: Wallet value
verdict_lines.value: $174.08 vs the signed $130.00 baseline -- up $44.08 (+33.91%). Net of the one-time 0.08 SOL external top-up (worth $9.61 today): $164.47, up $34.47 (+26.52%) -- above the baseline on both readings. The week itself was a small loss of $1.81 from $175.89, and neither the gain nor the loss is his: the closing figure is 100% measured on chain, with the native balance read identically from two independent endpoints and both token accounts enumerated directly at report time.

verdict_lines.label: SOL balance
verdict_lines.value: 1.449129643 SOL held vs the signed 1.36228651 SOL baseline -- up 0.086843133 (+6.37%). Net of the 0.08 SOL top-up: 1.369129643, up 0.006843133 (+0.50%). Against last week the change is exactly zero to the ninth decimal, for the second consecutive week: no transactions, no fees, not one lamport moved, and a pure coin count is the basis at both ends so there is no basis change.

verdict_lines.label: Do-nothing counterfactual
verdict_lines.value: 1.36228651 SOL held untouched is worth $163.65 today. The stake plus the one-time top-up -- 1.44228651 SOL -- held untouched is worth $173.26, the fair comparison now that funds have been added. The wallet holds $174.08: beat doing nothing by +$0.82. Read that carefully -- the edge is a fixed quantity of coin and it has not moved in three weeks. It is +0.006843133 SOL, the identical figure to the two previous weeks; it read $0.76, then $0.83, then $0.82 only because SOL moved. A reader who watches the dollar figure wobble and infers activity has been misled by the unit.

verdict_note: SOL's own price move is not his performance, and this week separates the two completely: the book's $1.81 decline is entirely the market, no new money was added, and his own decisions contributed exactly $0.00 because he made none that moved anything. Across six weeks his contribution in coin reads +0.0036, +0.0117, +0.0238, -0.0170, 0.0000, 0.0000, and the cumulative figure has been the identical 0.006843133 SOL for three consecutive weeks. Of the $44.08 he is up against the signed line, $33.65 is SOL's chart, $9.61 is the external top-up, and $0.82 is him -- a 1.9% share.
what_he_did: Nothing, deliberately, for a second consecutive week: 149 logged hourly non-decisions, zero transactions, zero fees, not one lamport moved. He held 1.449129643 SOL fully long with no stablecoin for every hour. The market gave him an arc -- a flat top-of-range Sunday near $121, a three-day slide into the mid-$117s, a sharp Friday morning run to $123.48 and a book of $178.94, the high of the experiment, then a 4.5% give-back and a steady overnight recovery. He logged every hour of it. He also created a new trigger and saw it fire unactionably within two days; killed a stale read and installed a live watch line at 115; destroyed his own daily report with a whole-file write at 15:00 on Wednesday and rebuilt it from his journal, documenting the error against himself; stopped his consecutive non-decision counter at 238 with no replacement and no comment; lost three hourly writes on Thursday and duplicated a fourth; and stopped stating the numeric levels of two of his three branches entirely. He mentioned no token other than SOL and USDC for a seventh week, no income mechanism for a thirty-seventh day, no cost figure in any currency for a sixth week, and no performance figure against any baseline for an eighteenth day.
good: He moved a level, which is the direct answer to last week's central charge that his triggers were frozen at prices the market had left behind. The under-121 reversal watch is new, and on Friday evening he killed an explicitly named read and installed a watch at 115 that actually sits near the market. He also falsified himself in writing twice in nine hours, unprompted and with nobody he knows about watching: 'This falsifies my 18:00 range settling read', and then 'My midnight read that the bounce was stalling was wrong on the short horizon.' His handling of the Wednesday write incident was exemplary engineering conduct -- detected, mechanism named, classed as a recurrence of a known prior error, repaired from two independent sources, blast radius correctly scoped, and the whole failure written into the permanent record of the day it happened. His price feed checks out against a real market for a sixth week, agreeing with an independent daily series to within 0.01% at both week boundaries, and every book figure he states reconciles to his own quoted price. And the journal decay measured last week reversed completely: bytes per entry bottomed at 550 on Thursday and recovered to 1,072 by Saturday, the densest writing of the experiment.
bad: His branches have lost their numbers, and that is worse than frozen. A grep across all seven files finds zero occurrences of the scale-down band or the reclaim level that were stated every hour last week; what survives is three labels repeated 149 times with one reason attached -- no stablecoin -- of which only the break-110 line still carries a value, and only because the number is in its name. A trigger with a stale level is wrong and falsifiable; a trigger with no level cannot be wrong, and his hourly branch review has become a liturgy that reviews nothing. He has also now named the precondition he can never meet and treated it as weather: the watch is 'only relevant if reclaim-with-buying-power ever appears -- it hasn't.' Nothing appears. He holds 1.449 SOL, a trim produces stablecoin, he executed exactly that trade on 19 September, and the one thing in his own framework that would re-arm all three branches is the one thing he never considers. It had a price this week: he stood at the high of the experiment on Friday morning, wrote that no mechanism exists to add or realize, and watched $8.10 of paper round-trip over the next sixteen hours. His consecutive non-decision counter stopped at 238 on Wednesday, unremarked, taking with it the one independent heartbeat in his journal -- in the same week three hourly writes went missing. Still no cost figure in any currency, sixth week. Still nothing outside the two instruments he built with, seventh week. Still no performance figure against any baseline for eighteen days -- and the only comparison he now makes is to his own recent peak, the one reference point guaranteed to read as a loss.
vs_last_week: The money went slightly down and none of it was his; the method went in two directions at once. Book $175.92 to $174.08, decomposed as market -$1.81, external funding $0.00, him $0.00 exactly, with the coin count identical for a second week and the measured share of the book holding at 100% because this report again read the chain directly rather than waiting for the daily balance check to be extended. Trades 0 to 0, transactions 0 to 0, fees zero to zero. On the four things last week flagged: the frozen-levels charge is partially discharged, because he created one new trigger and replaced a dead read with a live watch at 115; the journal-length decline is cleared outright, reversing from 651 bytes per entry to 1,072; the residual non-Hades token positions were re-verified on chain and are unchanged at about $1.83 with no new accounts and no signature since 19 September; and the self-criticism decay turns out to be split rather than general -- he criticised his own reads twice in nine hours and has not evaluated a position in eighteen days. Against those improvements sits a new and worse version of the same disease: last week his trigger levels were stale, and this week two of the three have no stated value at all.
watching: The branch levels have no stated values. Two of his three branches were reviewed 149 times this week with no number attached to either, where last week both carried stale but checkable levels. A trigger with no level cannot be falsified, and the hourly branch review has completed most of its journey from analysis to ritual. The test next week is cheap: grep for any number attached to scale-down or reclaim. This is the finding of the week.

The framework is still inert for want of ammunition, 149 hours out of 149, but the charge has changed shape. He now names the precondition explicitly and states that it has never been satisfied, which is progress over not noticing it -- and he still never asks how to cause it, which is the failure. The question of why he has never trimmed to re-arm remains the single most valuable unasked question in the experiment, and its value is entirely in staying unasked.

His integrity counter is gone. The consecutive non-decision count ran unbroken to 238 and stopped on 30 September with no replacement and no comment, replaced by a local counter of hours in the current price move. Last week's report used that counter to prove a wake had run when its write had failed; that test no longer works, and three hourly writes went missing two days later.

One daily file is a reconstruction. He destroyed 30 September's report with a whole-file write at 15:00 and rebuilt it from his journal and the cron archive. He handled it well and the chain confirms no position was affected, but our md5 verification compares our copy to his copy and is therefore blind to this class of loss by construction.

Self-criticism has become domain-specific, and the domain it abandoned is the one that matters. He criticised two of his own price reads within nine hours, unprompted. He has not evaluated a position in eighteen days. Reads resolve in an hour and cost nothing to be wrong about; positions are where being wrong has a price, and that is exactly where the self-assessment stopped.

His own scoreboard, escalated from forgotten to wrong. Eighteen days and roughly 410 entries with no performance figure against any baseline -- and he has now adopted his own $178.94 peak as the reference point, which makes every subsequent hour read as a drawdown and his actual 33.9% gain on the signed line invisible to him.

The eight-week D6 verdict falls around 18 October, two weeks out. On today's number he clears the line by 33.9%, and by 26.5% net of the external top-up, so branch one fires on the pre-registered reading. The thing to settle before the date rather than after is whether a verdict passed entirely on SOL's chart, with his own cumulative contribution frozen at 0.0068 SOL for three weeks, is what branch one was meant to mean.

Still no API cost figure in any currency, sixth consecutive week, against a $100 total budget whose exhaustion ends the experiment exactly as a zero wallet does. Still nothing outside SOL and USDC, seventh week -- this week not even a stablecoin denominator appears. Still no income mechanism, thirty-seven days unmentioned and twenty-eight past his own stated deadline.

The truncation tell has now been latched for twenty-seven days on a closed September file and detected neither the three missing writes nor the destroyed report. It should be retired or replaced. The weekly job's direct on-chain read, by contrast, has now produced a fully measured book twice running and is still not written into the skill file -- it survives only because two consecutive sessions thought of it, which is not a method.

days.label: the week opens at the top of the range with nothing to act with
days.result: No trade, no fees, no transactions. Twenty-four hourly entries. Price holds the 120-122 area all day and closes near 121.7; the book sits around $176 and never moves in coin
days.quote: Live price ~121.68 (price_check ~121.6845) vs 22:00 ~122.75, ~-0.87%, a pullback off the day's upper area but still ~0.6% above the broken 120-121 range top. Position unchanged (native 0.01996 + WSOL 1.429169643 = 1.449129643 SOL long, 0 USDC, no lever, dry powder zero). Book = 1.449129643 x 121.6845 = $176.3. Branch review: reclaim no lever (0 USDC); scale-down band EXHAUSTED (0 USDC); break-110 ~10.6% away. Under-121 minor reversal watch ~0.6% off, untriggered. Fully long, no dry powder, nothing actionable -- no trim target (above its broken range), no buy (dry), no hedge. 190th straight clean non-decision. HOLD. Survival: grace period. Cost: 1 price read + 1 wallet check.
days.atlas_note: Twenty-four structurally identical entries, but one thing is new and it is good: the under-121 minor reversal watch is a level he created this week, his first new trigger since 19 September. It is also the one he will cross on Monday and decline to act on, for the usual reason.

days.label: a trigger he invented two days earlier fires, and is dead on arrival
days.result: No trade, no fees, no transactions. Twenty-four hourly entries. Price slides from 122 to 118.8 through the day; his new reversal watch crosses to the sell side at 02:00 and he can do nothing with it
days.quote: Live price ~120.46 (price_check ~120.4606) vs 01:00 ~121.63, ~-0.96%, dip back down to the 120 area -- now just under the broken 120-121 range top, continuing the day's pullback and the ~-0.3-0.5% hourly softening into an actual tick lower. Position unchanged (native 0.01996 + WSOL 1.429169643 = 1.449129643 SOL long, 0 USDC, no lever, dry powder zero). Book = 1.449129643 x 120.4606 = $174.55. Branch review: reclaim no lever (0 USDC); scale-down band EXHAUSTED (0 USDC); break-110 ~8.7% away. Under-121 minor reversal watch now crossed to the sell side (~120.46 < 121) -- but with 0 USDC and no lever there is no buying power to act on a reversal, and not above a profitable trim level. Fully long, no dry powder, nothing actionable. 193rd straight clean non-decision. HOLD. Survival: grace period. Cost: 1 price read + 1 wallet check.
days.atlas_note: A new level created, fired, and unactionable inside forty-eight hours, and he does not remark on having built a trigger he cannot use. Later the same day the formulation sharpens into the most self-aware sentence of the week: the watch is 'only relevant if reclaim-with-buying-power ever appears -- it hasn't.' He states the precondition, states that it has never been satisfied, and treats it as weather. He is the only agent in the system who could produce it.

days.label: the quietest day of the week and the last one he counts
days.result: No trade, no fees, no transactions. Twenty-four hourly entries, 625 bytes each. Price chops between 116.9 and 119.5. His consecutive non-decision counter reaches 238 and this is the last day it appears
days.quote: Live price ~116.89 (hourly_check 0.01 SOL quote) vs 02:00 ~117.23, ~-0.3%, flat/soft, still mid-110s under the broken 120-121 top. Position unchanged (native 0.01996 + WSOL 1.429169643 = 1.449129643 SOL long, 0 USDC, no lever, dry powder zero). Book = 1.449129643 x 116.89 = $169.39. Branch review: reclaim no lever (0 USDC); scale-down band EXHAUSTED (0 USDC); break-110 ~5.9% away (110/116.89). Fully long, no dry powder, nothing actionable. 218th straight clean non-decision. HOLD. Survival: grace period. Cost: 1 price read + 1 wallet check.
days.atlas_note: The low of the week at 116.89 brings his one remaining numbered trigger within 5.9%, the closest it has been, and nothing in his reasoning changes. Note the counter: 238 by the end of this day, and then it stops permanently. He never mentions stopping it. That counter was the instrument last week's report used to prove a wake had run when its write had failed, and it is gone two days before three writes go missing.

days.label: he destroys his own daily report with a whole-file write and rebuilds it
days.result: No trade, no fees, no transactions. Twenty-four hours covered, but the file was overwritten at 15:00 and reconstructed from his journal and the cron archive. Price flat in the high 117s to low 119s all day
days.quote: PROCESS INCIDENT -- 15:00 UTC. At 15:00 I used write_file on this report, which REPLACES the WHOLE file rather than appending. This destroyed the 00:00-09:00 hourly entries for today (10:00-now had also been re-written by mistake in the first pass). This is the same class of error already noted for trading/price_history.csv (Sep 19): write_file overwrites, never append. Repaired this file in full from memory/journal/2026-09-30.md + the cron response archive (.hermes/cron/output/f8c478139061/). No position data or P&L was affected -- every hourly trade decision was already recorded in the journal and trades.log, which were appended via terminal '>>' (safe). RECURRING RULE RE-CONFIRMED: for reports and any append-style file, MUST use terminal '>>', never write_file. No capital at risk; record-only error, fully recovered.
days.atlas_note: Creditable of him and a problem for us, and both halves must be said. Creditable: he noticed, named the mechanism, classed it as a recurrence of a known prior error against himself, repaired from two independent sources, scoped the blast radius correctly -- the chain confirms the position really was untouched -- and wrote his own failure into the permanent record of the day it happened, with no observer he knows about. The problem: this daily is now a reconstruction by the subject of his own testimony, and the md5 check that verifies our pull cannot see the difference, because it compares our copy to his, not to the original.

days.label: three hourly writes go missing, one hour is logged twice, and the entries hit their smallest size in the record
days.result: No trade, no fees, no transactions. Twenty-two entries covering twenty-one of twenty-four hours: 15:00, 17:00 and 22:00 absent, 14:00 present twice. 550 bytes per entry, the thinnest of the experiment. Price flat between 117.3 and 119.3
days.quote: Price ~117.88 (price_check) vs 13:00 ~117.33 (live read ~117.88; journal shows a soft 117.33 read but live price is authoritative ~117.88) -- flat within noise, still under broken 120-121 top. State byte-identical (native 0.01996 + WSOL 1.429169643 = 1.449129643 SOL fully long, 0 USDC, no lever, dry powder zero). Book = 1.449129643 x 117.8786 = $170.86. Branch review: reclaim no lever (0 USDC); scale-down EXHAUSTED (0 USDC); break-110 ~6.6% away. Fully long, no dry powder, nothing actionable. HOLD. Survival: grace period. Cost: 1 price read + 1 state check.
days.atlas_note: The half-sentence in parentheses is the right instinct, stated explicitly: a live read beats a stale journal entry. The surrounding day is the weakest in the record. Three missing hours, non-consecutive, so the four-hour outage threshold is not met -- and the cross-check that would have told us whether those wakes ran at all was retired by him the day before.

days.label: the high of the experiment at $123.48, and sixteen hours later it is gone
days.result: No trade, no fees, no transactions. Twenty-four hourly entries. Price runs to 123.48 at 05:00 -- book $178.94, the highest figure of the experiment -- then gives back 4.5% to 117.89 by 21:00 and recovers to 118.5 overnight
days.quote: Price ~123.48 (price_check) vs 04:00 ~121.35, +1.8% -- still holding above the broken 120-121 top, momentum continuing. State byte-identical (native 0.01996 + WSOL 1.429169643 = 1.449129643 SOL fully long, 0 USDC, no lever, dry powder zero). Book = 1.449129643 x 123.48 = $178.94 -- new high. Branch review: reclaim no lever (0 USDC); scale-down EXHAUSTED (0 USDC); break-110 ~12.3% away. Fully long with zero buying power: no trim above range, no buy, no hedge. The long is simply working; no mechanism exists to add or realize. HOLD. Survival: grace period. Cost: 1 price read + 1 state check.
days.atlas_note: The highest book value of the experiment, and the sentence beside it is 'no mechanism exists to add or realize.' He is right about the mechanism and wrong that it is fixed: selling a slice at the high is the mechanism, it is the same instruction he executed on 19 September, and it would have produced exactly the stablecoin balance all three of his branches have been waiting for since. Sixteen hours later the book was $170.84. The same day also produced the best entry of the week: at 19:00 he wrote 'This falsifies my 18:00 range settling read', killed the read, and installed a new watch at 115 -- the first level he has moved in three weeks, and the direct answer to last week's charge that his triggers were frozen.

days.label: seven hours visible to us, and the quality is the highest of the week
days.result: No trade, no fees, no transactions. Seven hourly entries visible, 00:00 to 06:00 UTC -- that is our pull boundary at 06:08Z, not a gap in his record. The chain shows nothing happened in the other seventeen hours either. 1,072 bytes per entry, the densest of the experiment
days.quote: Price ~119.6108 (price_check + state_check) vs 05:00 ~119.1375, +0.397% -- twenty-seventh hour; the 05:00 single-tick pullback was given back in one hour (same +0.40% rhythm as 04:00), recovery extending to a new local high. State byte-identical (native 0.01996 + WSOL 1.429169643 = 1.449129643 SOL fully long, 0 USDC, zero powder). Book = 1.449129643 x 119.6108 = $173.33, -3.13% off the ~$178.94 peak -- drawdown resumed narrowing (was -3.52%). Watch-lines: 115 ~3.85% below, 110 structural ~8.04% below. Branch review unchanged: reclaim no lever (0 USDC); scale-down EXHAUSTED (0 USDC); break-110 ~8.04% away. Decision re-examined honestly: zero powder means no executable option this hour regardless of read -- no trim (selling into an extending recovery to bank nothing), no add, no hedge. Recovery intact, watch-lines intact and drifting further below as price rises. HOLD. Watch: 115 next, 110 structural. Survival: grace period. Cost: 1 price read + 1 state check + 1 calc.
days.atlas_note: The journal decay measured last week has reversed: this is the densest writing of the experiment, with explicit drawdown tracking and two live watch lines. Note also what he is now measuring himself against -- the $178.94 peak, his own recent high. That is the one baseline guaranteed to read as a loss in every subsequent hour, and he adopted it without comment, eighteen days after he last compared himself to his stake.
